A **Persian (Farsi)** fine-tune of [Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Audio8/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b), a 0.6B-parameter DualAR text-to-speech model with zero-shot voice cloning. | دیروز با دوستام رفتیم سینما، فیلمش واقعاً عالی بود! | [ft_s03.wav](samples/ft_s03.wav) |
| Voice clone (reference from a second speaker) | [clone_s01.wav](samples/clone_s01.wav) |

## Usage

The model uses Audio8's custom Transformers code (`trust_remote_code=True`). Normalize Persian text the same way as in training (digits → words, Arabic → Persian letters) with `normalize_fa` from the GitHub repo.

```python
# pip install "transformers>=4.57,<5" soundfile num2fawords
# git clone https://github.com/ard9/Audio8-Persian-TTS  (for fa_tools.normalize_fa)
import sys, torch, soundfile as sf
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor
sys.path.insert(0, "Audio8-Persian-TTS/src")
from fa_tools import normalize_fa

model_id = "ArminRahimi/Audio8-TTS-Persian"
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=dtype).eval().to(device)

text = normalize_fa("سلام! حال شما چطور است؟")
inputs = processor(text=[text], return_tensors="pt")
# Voice cloning: add reference_audio=["ref.wav"], reference_text=[normalize_fa("exact transcript")]
inputs = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in inputs.items()}
with torch.inference_mode():
    out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95, top_k=50,
                         do_sample=True, return_dict_in_generate=True)
    wav, lengths = model.decode_audio(out.codes)
sf.write("output.wav", wav[0, : int(lengths[0])].float().cpu().numpy(), model.config.codec_sample_rate)
```

Or from the command line: `python scripts/synthesize.py --model ArminRahimi/Audio8-TTS-Persian --text "سلام" --output out.wav`.

Keep each input under ~150 characters; `scripts/synthesize.py` splits longer text into sentences automatically.

## Training details

| | |
|---|---|
| Base model | Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6B (repo commit `07e40f5`) |
| Data | 33 of 77 Mana-TTS parts + GPTInformal-Persian: 31.6 h of audio after filtering (HIGH alignment quality only, 1–20 s clips) |
| Reference conditioning | ~30% of Mana-TTS rows and 100% of GPTInformal rows trained with a same-speaker reference clip |
| Trainable parameters | Both DualAR branches (slow + fast AR), all 601M parameters |
| Optimizer | 8-bit AdamW, lr 3e-5, cosine schedule, 3% warmup, grad-norm clip 1.0 |
| Precision | fp32 master weights + fp16 autocast (T4) |
| Effective batch size | 16 (batch 2 × gradient accumulation 8) |
| Steps / epochs | 7000 / 2 |
| Hardware | 1× T4 on Google Colab, several sessions resumed from Hub checkpoints |
| Exported weights | bf16 |

## Evaluation

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Eval loss (held-out, slow + fast AR) | 8.00 at step 7000 (v0.1, trained on 10 parts: 8.80; different eval split) |
| Listening impression | Intelligible Persian speech; prosody still somewhat robotic |
| CER, Whisper transcription of generated speech | not measured yet |
| MOS, native listeners | not measured yet |
| Speaker similarity (voice cloning) | not measured yet |

## Limitations

- **Mostly single-speaker data** (31.6 h after filtering: 33 of 77 Mana-TTS parts from one speaker + GPTInformal). Voice variety and prosody are limited; cloning of unseen voices is weaker than in Audio8's supported languages.
- **Limited compute** (a single Colab T4); no hyperparameter search.
- **No G2P**: unwritten short vowels, homographs and the ezafe can be mispronounced.
- Dates, abbreviations and Latin-script words are not specially normalized.
- The base model is a Preview checkpoint without Persian pre-training.
- Prosody still sounds somewhat robotic.

## Responsible use

This model can imitate voices. Clone a voice only with the speaker's explicit consent and disclose synthetic audio. Do not use it for impersonation, fraud or misinformation. The training data's authors prohibit using it to imitate their speakers' voices for malicious purposes.

Training data: [Mana-TTS](https://huggingface.co/datasets/MahtaFetrat/Mana-TTS) and [GPTInformal-Persian](https://huggingface.co/datasets/MahtaFetrat/GPTInformal-Persian) (CC0-1.0).

# WAXAL VoxCPM2 — Top-5 African TTS

A full fine-tune of [VoxCPM2](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/VoxCPM2) (2B params, tokenizer-free, diffusion-AR TTS with voice cloning) on the **5 highest-resource languages** in the WAXAL/AfroNet collection, produced by the [WAXAL](https://huggingface.co/waxal-benchmarking) project at [LyngualLabs](https://lynguallabs.org).

This is a research checkpoint. It is not production-polished — see **Known Limitations** below before using it for anything beyond experimentation.

This is the first model in the collection trained on a **cleaned** version of the WAXAL/AfroNet pooled corpus (see **Data Cleaning** below) rather than the raw pooled data used for earlier releases like `voxcpm2-multilang28-full`. It's also the smallest of three sibling models (Top-5 / Top-10 / all-28) trained from the same cleaned data and methodology, to compare whether language count or data quality matters more at this scale.

## Languages

VoxCPM2 has no built-in mechanism for specifying language at inference — the base model infers pronunciation purely from text orthography. We use a dedicated `<lang:XX>` tag per language, registered as a real token in the tokenizer and resized into the text embedding table (mean-initialized, then learned during fine-tuning). **The tag is mandatory** — always prepend it to the text you want synthesized, e.g.:

```
<lang:yo> Ẹ káàárọ̀! Báwo ni oorun rí lálẹ́ àná?
```

| Language | Tag | Hours after cleaning | Hours after resampling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Swahili | `<lang:sw>` | 922.8 | 833.2 |
| Kinyarwanda | `<lang:rw>` | 910.5 | 827.6 |
| Yoruba | `<lang:yo>` | 732.3 | 742.2 |
| Igbo | `<lang:ig>` | 620.2 | 683.1 |
| Hausa | `<lang:ha>` | 534.2 | 633.9 |

Source data: the [AfroNet](https://huggingface.co/Professor) speech collection (`Professor/<language>-speech-data`), after the Phase 1 cleaning pass described below. These tags are a subset of the 10 registered in `VoxCPM2_langtagged` (the same tagged base used for the Top-10 sibling model); the other 5 tag embedding rows exist in this checkpoint's vocabulary but received no training signal here.

## Data Cleaning

Earlier releases in this collection (`voxcpm2-multilang28-full`, `voxcpm2-multilang10-full`, `voxcpm2-bantu8-full`) trained directly on the pooled raw corpus. This model and its Top-10 / all-28 siblings are trained on data that first passed through a dedicated cleaning pipeline, applied per language before any resampling:

1. **Clip/peak check** — reject clips with a sustained near-full-scale amplitude (likely clipped/distorted audio).
2. **Silence trim** — trim leading/trailing silence (RMS-threshold based) before any downstream check, so later checks evaluate the audio that's actually used for training, not the untrimmed original.
3. **Duration-vs-text-length ratio check** — flag clips whose trimmed duration is a statistical outlier relative to their text length for that language (1st/99th percentile bounds). This caught a real upstream data bug: a small number of rows (worst case, a single 9-second clip in the Luganda corpus) had their `text` field corrupted with multiple concatenated Common Voice metadata records — up to 225,940 characters for one clip. This check strips that kind of corruption out before it reaches training.
4. **ASR-CER gate** — transcribe the trimmed audio with a small ASR model (`omniASR_CTC_1B`) and compare against the label text (CER threshold 0.3, diacritic/tone-mark-insensitive comparison so correct transcriptions aren't penalized for missing a tone mark the ASR doesn't produce).

Retention for this model's 5 languages after cleaning: Swahili 96.4%, Kinyarwanda 96.1%, Hausa 82.0%, Yoruba 74.0%, Igbo 69.6%. Yoruba and Igbo's lower retention is primarily genuine ASR-CER disagreement rather than bad data — both are tonal/diacritic-heavy languages where `omniASR_CTC_1B` performs less reliably; see **Known Limitations**.

## Training

- **Base**: `VoxCPM2_langtagged` — `openbmb/VoxCPM2` with 10 `<lang:XX>` tokens added and the text embedding table resized (mean-initialized rows) before any fine-tuning. This is the same tagged base reused for the Top-10 sibling model; this run only trains on data for 5 of its 10 registered tags.
- **Mode**: full fine-tuning (all parameters trainable except the frozen AudioVAE codec).
- **Data balancing**: sqrt-temperature resampling (weight ∝ √hours, renormalized to preserve total volume) across the 5 languages, same methodology as the other models in this collection.
- **Scale**: 2,217,874 training rows (clips) after resampling, 3,230 held-out validation rows.
- **Steps**: 34,000 steps (~1.01 epochs over the resampled training set), batch size 3 × grad-accum 11 × 2 GPUs (effective batch 66).
- **Hardware**: 2× NVIDIA H200, via `torchrun` DDP.
- **Learning rate**: 1e-5, 100 warmup steps.
- **Final validation loss**: total 0.838 (diff 0.822, stop 0.017) at step 33,999.

## Usage

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
from voxcpm import VoxCPM
import soundfile as sf

model_dir = snapshot_download("waxal-benchmarking/voxcpm2-top5-full")
model = VoxCPM.from_pretrained(model_dir, load_denoiser=False, optimize=False)

wav = model.generate(
    text="<lang:sw> Habari ya asubuhi! Leo ni siku nzuri sana.",
    cfg_value=2.0,
    inference_timesteps=22,
)
sf.write("out.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate)
```

`optimize=False` is required — `torch.compile` (the default optimization path) conflicts with some inference environments (e.g. HF ZeroGPU Spaces); disabling it costs some speed but avoids crashes.

Voice cloning works the same way as base VoxCPM2 — pass `prompt_wav_path` and `prompt_text` (the literal transcript of what's spoken in the reference clip) alongside the tagged `text`.

## Evaluation

**Pending.** The automated evaluation pipeline used for earlier releases (ASR-based CER against ground-truth text, a real-recording CER noise floor per language, and DNSMOS naturalness) has not yet been run against this checkpoint. Numbers from `voxcpm2-multilang28-full` are **not applicable here** — that model was trained on uncleaned data with a different language set and is not a valid proxy for this model's quality. This section will be updated once Stage A/B/C evaluation has run.

## Known Limitations

- **No evaluation results yet** (see above) — training loss converging normally is not the same as verified downstream speech quality.
- **Yoruba and Igbo retained less data than the other three languages** (74.0% and 69.6% vs. 96%+ for Swahili/Kinyarwanda) due to the ASR-CER gate disagreeing more often on these tonal/diacritic-heavy languages. We did not disable the CER gate for these two (unlike Somali/Ikposo in the all-28 cleaning pass, where drop rates were far more extreme at 70-80%) — their elevated-but-not-extreme drop rates were judged plausible rather than clearly an ASR-model artifact, but this is a judgment call, not a certainty.
- **Voice-design and cross-lingual flexibility are likely reduced**, consistent with what we've seen in other full-fine-tune checkpoints in this collection — full-FT on read-speech-only data tends to degrade the base model's text-prompted style/voice-design control and non-trained-language generation.
- **Non-terminating generation** was an observed failure mode in earlier releases on this same base model (see `voxcpm2-multilang28-full`'s model card); whether it recurs here is one of the things the pending evaluation will check.
- Only 5 of the 10 tag embedding rows present in this checkpoint's vocabulary (inherited from the shared `VoxCPM2_langtagged` base) received any training signal — do not use the other 5 tags with this checkpoint.

## Related

- [`waxal-benchmarking/voxcpm2-multilang28-full`](https://huggingface.co/waxal-benchmarking/voxcpm2-multilang28-full) and [`voxcpm2-multilang10-full`](https://huggingface.co/waxal-benchmarking/voxcpm2-multilang10-full) — earlier releases trained on the uncleaned pooled corpus.
- Top-10 and all-28 (clean-data) sibling models — trained the same way as this one, for comparison; linked here once released.
- [AfroNet speech collection](https://huggingface.co/Professor) — the source training data.

# Drama 3 for MLX — mixed 3-bit (measured)

> **This checkpoint now lives at [mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-3bit](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-3bit).** The files are the same; use that repo for updates. Drama 3 support is merged into mlx-audio ([#1018](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio/pull/1018)).

**Built with Fish Audio.**

An MLX conversion of [Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3) for Apple Silicon: routed experts at **3 bits**, dense projections and the audio tower at **8 bits**. In our tests it matched 8-bit quality while being the smallest setting that kept quality — 18.5 GB on disk, about 22.5–24 GB peak while generating, so it fits a **32 GB Mac**.

This is an unofficial community conversion. It is not released or endorsed by Fish Audio.

## Quality, measured

20 voice-cloned English clips (10 sentences × 2 seeds), M5 Max. Whisper large-v3-turbo word error rate, ECAPA speaker similarity to a held-out clip of the reference speaker, UTMOS. "Failed" = WER above 20 % or no end of speech.

| Experts / dense | Backbone | WER | Failed | Speaker sim | UTMOS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 / 8 | 34.3 GB | 1.6 % | 0/20 | 0.625 | 3.92 |
| 4 / 8 | 19.3 GB | 2.5 % | 0/20 | 0.619 | 3.92 |
| **3 / 8 (this model)** | **16.9 GB** | **1.4 %** | **0/20** | **0.610** | **4.04** |
| 2 / 8 | 11.8 GB | 0.9 % | 0/20 | 0.624 | 3.84 |
| 3 / 3 | 14.1 GB | 26.7 % | 9/20 | 0.561 | 3.13 |

- The row for this model was measured on this exact checkpoint through mlx-audio. Other rows come from the same sweep in a standalone MLX port.
- In a blind listening test (6 lines × 3 versions), the listener did not prefer 8-bit over this model.
- 2-bit experts dropped the last two lines of a multi-speaker dialogue, so they are not offered here.
- Also checked on this setting: two-speaker dialogue, `[sighs]` / `[laughs]` cues, Hinglish, Hindi and a 43 s long-form script.

## Usage

Drama 3 support is merged into mlx-audio ([#1018](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio/pull/1018)). Until it is in a release, install from `main`:

```bash
pip install "mlx-audio[tts] @ git+https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio"
```

```python
from mlx_audio.tts.utils import load_model

model = load_model("mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-3bit")
for result in model.generate(
    text="<|speaker:0|> So what did you ship this week? <|speaker:1|> [laughs] A spreadsheet.",
    ref_audio="reference.wav",
    ref_text="Transcript of the reference clip.",
):
    audio = result.audio  # 44.1 kHz
```

Speed: about 36 frames/s on an M5 Max (1.7× real time). Rebuild it yourself with:

```bash
python -m mlx_audio.tts.models.fish_drama3.convert --src drama-3 --dst drama-3-mlx-mixed-3bit \
    --expert-bits 3 --dense-bits 8 --tower-bits 8
```

# Shtorm-PocketTTS-RU v2 «версия 2, 01.10.2026»

Русская модель для [pocket-tts](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts) (Kyutai),
заточенная под **чтение книг**: ровная книжная подача, живая интонация,
клонирование голоса по короткому рефу.

> Запускайте по примеру из раздела [Запуск](#запуск). Автоматический пример в кнопке
> «Use this model» использует английский текст и английский голос — латиница моделью
> пока не поддерживается.

- архитектура оригинального pocket-tts: 6 слоёв, ~100M параметров — быстро и на CPU;
- токенизатор SentencePiece на русском корпусе (4000 токенов), общий для обеих моделей.

## Две модели: fast и slow

Разница в подаче, а не в качестве:

- **fast** (`config_fast.yaml`, он же `config.yaml`) — бодрее и живее: шире интонация,
  медленные голоса не тянут. На быстрых голосах может строчить.
- **slow** (`config_slow.yaml`) — спокойнее: свободнее паузы, ровнее тон.
  На медленных голосах может тянуть.

На одной и той же главе разница около 7% по времени (11:01 против 11:48).
Это замер на голосе с длинными паузами — на более быстрых голосах разница между моделями будет уменьшаться.
Какая лучше — зависит от голоса и вкуса, попробуйте обе.

## Предыдущие версии

**v1 (26.09.2026)** — первая версия: спокойная, размеренная книжная подача.
Подача спокойнее и ровнее, чем у v2, но на медленных голосах и длинных фразах
может «тянуть» и затухать к концу куска. Если она вам нравилась больше — она
никуда не делась: файлы в папке [`v1/`](https://huggingface.co/ArtShtorm/Shtorm-PocketTTS-RU/tree/main/v1),
запуск через `v1/config.yaml`.

Токенизатор у v1 и v2 одинаковый.

## Цифры

Замеры **v1**, 7 голосов x 5 сидов, книжный абзац / диалог:

| CER (разборчивость) | UTMOS (качество звука) | обрывы |
|---|---|---|
| 1.6% / 4.0% | 3.64 / 3.52 | 0 из 70 |

## Запуск

```python
from pocket_tts import TTSModel
import scipy.io.wavfile

# fast (по умолчанию):
model = TTSModel.load_model(config="hf://ArtShtorm/Shtorm-PocketTTS-RU/config.yaml")
# slow — спокойная подача:
# model = TTSModel.load_model(config="hf://ArtShtorm/Shtorm-PocketTTS-RU/config_slow.yaml")

voice = model.get_state_for_audio_prompt("my_voice.wav")
audio = model.generate_audio(voice, "Се́рое не́бо висе́ло над го́родом.")
scipy.io.wavfile.write("out.wav", model.sample_rate, audio.numpy())
```

Советы:

- **ударения** — знаком акута (U+0301), как в примере: модель училась на размеченном тексте;
- **реф** — 5 с чистой речи, законченная фраза: модель копирует из него тембр, темп и полосу;
- **куски до ~120-180 знаков**: на длинных громкость к концу проседает;
- **латиница пока не поддерживается** — английские слова и цифры перед синтезом нужно
  нормализовать (записать по-русски). Поддержка латиницы — в планах.

## Ограничения

- паузы на знаках препинания местами длинноваты;
- на длинных кусках — затухание громкости (лечится выравниванием громкости на выходе).

Клонирование голоса — только с явного согласия его владельца; не использовать для
выдачи себя за другого человека, дезинформации и иного вредного или незаконного использования.

# OmniVoice for WebGPU, compact

A browser build of [OmniVoice](https://huggingface.co/k2-fsa/OmniVoice) (Han Zhu et al., k2-fsa / Xiaomi) for
ONNX Runtime Web on WebGPU. All weights are gzip-compressed; decompress them with `DecompressionStream('gzip')`
before creating a session.

| Profile | Files | Download |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Speech | `llm_decoder_int4`, `audio_embeddings_encoder`, `audio_heads_decoder`, `tokenizer.json`, `codec/higgs_decoder` | ~358 MB |
| Voice cloning (once per voice) | `codec/acoustic_encoder`, `codec/semantic_encoder`, `codec/quantizer_encoder` | ~107 MB |

## Sources and changes

- `llm_decoder_int4.onnx`: the bidirectional-attention re-export from
  [PranavBoi/omnivoice-web](https://huggingface.co/PranavBoi/omnivoice-web) at `53e33f3b`, unchanged apart from gzip.
- `audio_embeddings_encoder.onnx`, `audio_heads_decoder.onnx` (int4), `tokenizer.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`:
  [onnx-community/OmniVoice-Onnx](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/OmniVoice-Onnx) at `a7be7c65`, unchanged
  apart from gzip.
- `codec/*`: the fp32 Higgs Audio v2 tokenizer from onnx-community at `a7be7c65`, converted here:
  - weights of Conv, ConvTranspose and MatMul layers stored as per-channel symmetric int8 with
    `DequantizeLinear`; the remaining large weights stored as float16 with a `Cast` to float32;
  - the semantic encoder's MatMul layers quantized to 4 bits (`MatMulNBits`, block 32, symmetric);
  - activations stay float32. The published fp16 codec overflows on WebGPU (non-finite output from the acoustic
    encoder and the decoder) and its semantic encoder does not load in ONNX Runtime.

## Measurements

Speaker similarity (WeSpeaker ResNet34, cosine) between a cloned output and its reference clip, three reference
voices (two French, one English), same seed, CPU execution provider:

| Codec | Size | Similarity |

# AudioDeepFake-Detecter (laogao fine-tune)

Binary classifier for synthetic vs. real speech, built on [DistilHuBERT](https://huggingface.co/ntu-spml/distilhubert).
Code: https://github.com/zLiGhTKz/AudioDeepFake-Detecter

## Training
1. DistilHuBERT fine-tuned on the ASVspoof dataset for bona fide vs. spoofed speech.
2. Further fine-tuned on recordings of a single speaker ("laogao") and synthetic clips of that voice.

Labels: `0 = fake`, `1 = real`. Input: 16 kHz mono audio, scored in 1-second windows.

## Limitations
- Because of step 2, the model is specialised toward one speaker. It has **not** been evaluated on other speakers or on public benchmarks, and no accuracy figures are claimed.
- Not suitable as sole evidence in any high-stakes decision.

## Usage
```python
from transformers import pipeline
clf = pipeline("audio-classification", model="lightk/audiodeepfake-detecter-laogao")
print(clf("speech.wav"))
```
Or with the package: `audiodeepfake-detect speech.wav --model lightk/audiodeepfake-detecter-laogao`.
